name: Fire
summary: Fire 0.6.2: a design system for developer, agent and AI products, in its default look (the Ember palette, Geist and Geist Mono). Plain HTML and CSS are the contract: classes fd-*, variants and states through data-* and ARIA, tokens --fd-*. Light and dark values are exact; this content is generated from contract/fire-contract.json and contract/catalog.json, so edit the theme record (facet/theme.json), not these tokens.

muted.$description: Fire --fd-text-3 (an alpha token) laid over --fd-bg, so the value is opaque.

touch.$description: The default control on a coarse pointer (Fire grows --fd-control-md to 40px there).

motion.notes: Fire collapses every duration through one token: under prefers-reduced-motion it sets --fd-motion to 0 and --fd-press-scale to 1, and each duration is the token times --fd-motion, so nothing animates. Looping spinners and shimmers stop with it.

components.name: Button
components.purpose: The native button in Fire's soft style: a quiet fill that darkens on hover, with one primary per view. Variants and sizes are data attributes; loading, held and disabled come from aria-busy, aria-pressed, aria-expanded and disabled. On touch devices every size grows to a 40px target.

do: An action runs on this page and nothing navigates: save, create, send, copy, retry.
A dialog, sheet or confirmation needs its confirm and cancel actions.
A toolbar needs icon-only actions (add data-icon-only and an aria-label).
dont: The action is a link to another page, or sits inside a sentence. The text button (fd-btn-text), part of this component.
Several related actions belong together as one control. The button group (fd-btn-group), part of this component.
One floating action stays visible while the page scrolls. Use Fab.
The user picks one option of several, or switches a setting on and off. Use Segmented.
Delete or revoke runs without a confirmation step. Put it behind a dialog or confirm; use the danger variant on the confirming button.

Actions align right with the primary last; a destructive action sits alone at the left. data-fd-dirty shows a sticky unsaved-changes bar.
components.usage: Lay out fields and actions in a form that stays readable. Also called: settings form, form layout, form container, edit form.
do: A settings or create page holds several fields with a Save action.
Changes should trigger an unsaved-changes bar (data-fd-dirty, data-variant="sticky").
dont: A long form has titled groups that people scan. Use FormSection.
One setting is a label and a control on a row of a list. Use Setting.
A short form belongs in a modal. Use Dialog.
The form is a chat message. Use Composer.

props.name: size
props.description: Sets data-size. A narrow form such as an invite or a sign-in.

parts.name: children
parts.description: Slot: the component's content, given as the children of <cc-component>.

parts.name: form-row
parts.description: One setting: text left, control right.

parts.name: form-cols
parts.description: Columns of fields that fill the body.

parts.name: form-actions-text
parts.description: Text shown beside the actions, such as "Unsaved changes".

components.name: Meter
components.purpose: A thin bar that shows use against a limit. Set data-value and data-max; the fill, the colour and the ARIA meter role follow. It turns warning from 80% and danger from 95%. Segmented meters split use by category and take colours from the chart palette. The figures are the real information; the bar is the glance.
components.usage: Show how much of a limit is used. Also called: gauge, quota bar, usage bar, capacity, fuel gauge, level bar, limit bar.
do: A quota, a credit balance or a rate limit has a cap.
A table cell shows use next to the number: use the inline variant.
Use splits across categories: use the segmented variant with a legend.
dont: Work moving toward done. Use Progress.
A share of a whole with two to five parts. Use Donut.
A ranking of items by size. Use Bars.
A value over time. Use Chart.

props.name: variant
props.description: Sets data-variant. Bar and figure on one line, for table cells.

props.name: size
props.description: Sets data-size. A thinner bar in dense rows.

props.name: tone
props.description: Sets data-tone. A bar in ink when the accent is spoken for.

props.name: level
props.description: Sets data-level.

props.name: series
props.description: Sets data-series. A segment in the first chart colour.

parts.name: meter-seg
parts.description: One category of a segmented meter.

parts.name: meter-legend
parts.description: The legend of a segmented meter.

components.name: Slider
components.purpose: A styled native range input, so touch, arrow keys, Home/End and Page keys work. The accent fills to the thumb and a value bubble shows while dragging or when focused by keyboard. data-labels on the wrapper gives named stops with clickable ticks. Show the value in the label row so people do not guess from the thumb.
components.usage: Pick a position on a scale by dragging. Also called: range, range input, scrubber, track bar.
do: The value is a position on a scale and a rough setting is enough: effort, volume, depth.
Named stops such as Low, Medium, High suit the choice (data-variant="steps").
dont: The exact number matters. Use Number.
There are two to four named options with no scale. Use Segmented.
Progress is shown, not set. Use Progress.

props.name: variant
props.description: Sets data-variant. A few named stops with clickable ticks (data-labels).

props.name: bubble
props.description: Sets data-bubble.

parts.name: slider-bubble
parts.description: The value shown above the thumb while dragging.

parts.name: slider-ticks
parts.description: Clickable stop labels under the track.

parts.name: slider-value
parts.description: A visible value mirrored from the input.

components.name: Toast
components.purpose: A short message at the bottom right (bottom centre on phones) that stacks, fans out on hover and fades. Created with toast({ title, description, tone, action }); toast.promise follows a promise. It never asks a question. Toasts last 5 seconds, 8 for errors; loading lasts until settled. The stack is a polite live region.
components.usage: Confirm something that already happened, then get out of the way. Also called: snackbar, flash message, growl, notification toast, alert toast, sonner, message.
do: An action finished and needs a quiet receipt: key copied, saved, deleted.
Something finished elsewhere: a crawl completed, a webhook failed.
A long task needs a loading toast that turns into the result.
dont: The reader must choose or confirm something. Use Dialog.
A persistent warning next to content. Use Callout.
A notice about the whole account. Use Banner.
A list of past events to read later. Use Notification.

props.name: tone
props.description: Sets data-tone. A plain confirmation.

props.name: staticDemo
props.description: Sets data-static-demo.

parts.name: children
parts.description: Slot: the component's content, given as the children of <cc-component>.

parts.name: toaster
parts.description: The stack, a manual popover and live region.

parts.name: toast-progress
parts.description: The thin line showing the time left.

components.name: Bars
components.purpose: A list for a ranking: label left, a thin bar, the figure right in mono. It is plain CSS driven by one custom property per row, --value, a fraction from 0 to 1 of the longest row. Below 320px the bar drops under its label. The fill grows once when scrolled into view.
components.usage: Rank items by size: credits by endpoint, requests by key. Also called: bar list, ranked list, leaderboard, horizontal bars, top list, bar ranking, progress list.
do: A ranking of a few to a dozen items with exact figures.
Parts of a total where order matters more than proportion.
dont: Values over time. Use Chart.
Parts of a whole with two to five segments. Use Donut.
Use against a limit. Use Meter.
Rows with several columns. Use Table.

props.name: tone
props.description: Sets data-tone. A bar the one series that matters, in the accent.

components.name: Checklist
components.purpose: The body of a filter popover: a search row, checkable rows with counts, a summary and Clear. The trigger label summarises the choice. Each change fires fd:change with the selected values. Used inside a popover marked data-fd-filter-list.
components.usage: Pick several values from a long list, with search and counts. Also called: multi-select, filter list, checkbox list, faceted filter, multiselect, select many.
do: People filter by several values out of a long list: endpoints, keys, statuses.
Each option has a count worth showing.
dont: One choice from a short list. Use Menu.
A short set of options that all fit on the page. Use Choice.
A single filter chip that opens a menu. Use Filter.
Free-form values typed by the user. Use TagInput.

parts.name: children
parts.description: Slot: the component's content, given as the children of <cc-component>.

parts.name: checklist-count
parts.description: A muted count at the end of the row.

components.name: Codefield
components.purpose: A text area in the code face with a head showing the language and an optional Format button. Tab inserts two spaces. data-fd-json checks the value on blur and on submit and writes the parser's reason and line into the field's error. Without script it is a plain text area. It is for the few places raw code is the input, never a stand-in for a control that fits better.
components.usage: Edit raw code or JSON that has to be valid. Also called: code editor, JSON editor, config editor, monospace textarea.
do: An expert overrides configuration by hand and the value is JSON.
The input is code and needs checking: a template, a schema, a config override.
dont: The value is a list, a map or a choice that a control fits. Use TagInput.
The value is a map of names to values. Use Pairs.
The text is prose. Use Textarea.
The code is shown, not edited. Use Codeblock.

props.name: codefieldFormat
props.description: Sets data-fd-codefield-format.

parts.name: children
parts.description: Slot: the component's content, given as the children of <cc-component>.

parts.name: codefield-head
parts.description: Row with the language and the Format button.

components.name: DataCard
components.purpose: A framed block: a heading and description on the left, the figure and its unit opposite, and a toggle that reveals more (a table, a breakdown). It is the pattern behind "Credits remaining". The toggle sets aria-expanded and fires fd:open or fd:close.
components.usage: Show one figure with its context and keep the detail one click away. Also called: stat card, metric card, KPI card, summary card, balance card, figure card.
do: One number matters most and its breakdown belongs behind a click: credits left, balance, quota.
The detail is a small table or list that explains the figure.
dont: Several headline numbers side by side. Use Stats.
A figure that is use against a limit. Use Meter.
A generic object card. Use Card.
The detail is long prose. Use Accordion.

parts.name: children
parts.description: Slot: the component's content, given as the children of <cc-component>.

parts.name: data-card-unit
parts.description: The unit beside the number, in mono.

parts.name: data-card-toggle
parts.description: The button that reveals the detail.

components.name: FileUpload
components.purpose: A dashed, sunken area that is also a button: click or press Enter to browse, or drop files. Dragging over it turns the line accent. Accepted files appear as rows in fd-filelist with progress, status and size. fd:files is cancelable so your app can run the upload and report progress with setFileProgress(); data-max-mb and accept reject files that do not fit.
components.usage: Add files by dropping them or browsing. Also called: dropzone, file picker, file input, drag and drop upload, attachment.
do: People attach one or several files, such as a sitemap, a CSV or a document.
Upload progress and per-file errors should show as rows.
dont: One small file is chosen as part of a plain form and no progress is needed. Use Input.
The upload is an image avatar. Use Avatar.
Files are only listed, not added. Use List.

props.name: layout
props.description: Sets data-layout. A compact one-line dropzone in a form row.

parts.name: children
parts.description: Slot: the component's content, given as the children of <cc-component>.

parts.name: dropzone
parts.description: The drop area; a label around the file input.

parts.name: dropzone-icon
parts.description: The icon that lifts on drag.

parts.name: file-status
parts.description: Progress, ready or the reason it failed.

components.name: FormSection
components.purpose: One titled group in a long create or edit form: a narrow head with a title and one line on the left (it stays in view while the body scrolls) and the fields on a white surface beside it. Below about 720px of form width the head stacks above the body. Use it inside a form with data-size="full".
components.usage: Group the fields of a long form under a title. Also called: fieldset, form group, settings section, form card.
do: A create or edit form has more than one group: Basics, Callbacks, Access, Advanced.
People should scan titles and skip what they do not need.
dont: The form is short. Use Form.
A card holds a single setting with a control. Use Setting.
The groups are steps in a flow. Use Steps.

props.name: layout
props.description: Sets data-layout. The head stays above the body at every width.

parts.name: children
parts.description: Slot: the component's content, given as the children of <cc-component>.

parts.name: form-section-body
parts.description: The white surface holding the fields.

components.name: Heatgrid
components.purpose: A grid of day cells: weeks run in columns, Monday to Sunday in rows. Five steps run from a faint ink wash to the full accent, cut at the quartiles of the busy days so one spike does not flatten the rest. The strip variant shows one row of days with a tone each and a legend, for pass, slow or fail.
components.usage: See activity over weeks, one cell per day, or an outcome per day. Also called: calendar heatmap, contribution graph, activity grid, heat map, github graph, uptime strip, status strip.
do: Activity over weeks or months: requests, commits, runs per day.
Each day has an outcome, not an amount: use the strip with a legend.
A table cell needs the last 14 days at a glance: strip at data-size="sm".
dont: A value that changes by the hour or the minute. Use Chart.
A single day or week. Use Bars.
One quantity against a limit. Use Meter.
Exact numbers for each day. Use Table.

props.name: variant
props.description: Sets data-variant. One outcome per day: passed, slow, failed; no axis.

props.name: size
props.description: Sets data-size. 11px cells, or a strip for a table cell.

props.name: tone
props.description: Sets data-tone. A heat grid in green, for healthy runs.

parts.name: heatgrid-month
parts.description: A month label above the grid.

parts.name: heatgrid-day
parts.description: A weekday label beside the grid.

components.name: Listbox
components.purpose: The option list a combobox opens, and the list inside any picker: fd-option rows with a check for the selected one, an optional description and mono meta, group labels and an empty message. The active row is marked with data-active. It is a popover that falls back to an absolute panel where the Popover API is missing.
components.usage: Show a list of options a person can choose from. Also called: option list, dropdown list, picker list, suggestions list.
do: Building a picker or menu whose rows are choices with state (selected, active).
Rows need a description, an icon or a mono meta beside the label.
dont: A user needs a ready-made field with typing and filtering. Use Combobox.
The rows are actions, not choices. Use Menu.
The rows are plain choices from a short list. Use Select.
The rows are checkboxes or radios in a form. Use Checkbox.

props.name: side
props.description: Sets data-side. The list opens above its field, when there is no room below.

parts.name: children
parts.description: Slot: the component's content, given as the children of <cc-component>.

parts.name: options
parts.description: The list of rows, also used for checkbox groups.

parts.name: option-check
parts.description: The check on the selected option.

parts.name: listbox-empty
parts.description: The message when no option matches.

components.name: Number
components.purpose: A number input with steppers inside the field. Hold a stepper to repeat; steppers disable at min and max. Arrow keys and typing still work. fd:change fires with the new value.
components.usage: Enter a number and nudge it up or down. Also called: stepper, spinner, quantity input, numeric input.
do: The value is a count or an amount with limits: retries, page depth, seats.
People change it by small steps more than they type it.
dont: The value sits on a scale and exact digits matter less than position. Use Slider.
The number has a unit that should show beside it. Use InputGroup.
The value is an ID, a phone number or a code of digits. Use Input.
The code is sent to the person and entered once. Use Otp.

props.name: size
props.description: Sets data-size. A dense row (28px).

props.name: block
props.description: Sets data-block. The control fills its row.

props.name: fit
props.description: Sets data-fit. A short number; the width follows the input.

props.name: mono
props.description: Sets data-mono.

parts.name: number-step
parts.description: The minus and plus buttons (data-fd-step="-1" or "1").

components.name: Pairs
components.purpose: For OAuth scopes and their labels, request headers, environment variables. Each pair is a row with its own remove button. Without script it is a text area of "name = value" lines; with it, rows and one hidden input post the same lines or a JSON object (data-format="json"). A name used twice marks both invalid and stops the form posting.
components.usage: Edit a set of names with values as rows. Also called: key-value editor, key value input, headers editor, env vars editor, map editor.
do: The value is a map: scopes, headers, labels, environment variables.
The server stores an object and nobody should type JSON.
dont: The value is a flat list. Use TagInput.
The value is one setting with a fixed name. Use Field.
The data is a table people read and sort. Use Table.
Raw config is the actual input. Use Codefield.

props.name: size
props.description: Sets data-size. A compact editor.

props.name: format
props.description: Sets data-format.

props.name: mono
props.description: Sets data-mono. Names are identifiers and values are prose, as in scopes.

parts.name: children
parts.description: Slot: the component's content, given as the children of <cc-component>.

components.name: Sparkline
components.purpose: A tiny line or bar shape drawn from data-values. It is a shape, not a reading: put it beside a figure. With no data-tone it colours itself by trend, up as success and down as danger; data-invert flips that where lower is better. data-type="bars" draws bars; data-area fills under the line; data-dot ends it on a dot.
components.usage: Show the direction of a number in a few pixels beside it. Also called: mini chart, trend line, inline chart, microchart, sparkbar, tiny chart.
do: A stat tile, table cell or list row shows a number and its recent trend.
There is no room for axes or a tooltip.
dont: Readers need exact values or a time axis. Use Chart.
A ranking. Use Bars.
One value against a limit. Use Meter.
One outcome per day. Use Heatgrid.

props.name: tone
props.description: Sets data-tone. A fixed accent line, ignoring the trend.

props.name: fluid
props.description: Sets data-fluid. The sparkline fills the width of its container.

props.name: trend
props.description: Sets data-trend. Force the trend colour for a rising good value.

props.name: type
props.description: Sets data-type.

parts.name: sparkline-bar
parts.description: One bar of the bar type.

parts.name: sparkline-stop
parts.description: A gradient stop of the area fill.

components.name: Subnav
components.purpose: The side navigation inside settings: a 280px column of 40px rows. When it cannot sit beside the content (a container under 760px) it turns into a row of pills that scrolls sideways. Links navigate; buttons get aria-current="true" on click. fd:change fires on selection.
components.usage: Move between settings pages from a side column. Also called: settings nav, side nav, secondary navigation, vertical nav, local navigation.
do: A settings or account area has four or more pages and a column beside them.
The list stays visible while the page content changes.
dont: The whole app needs navigation. Use Sidebar.
The items are views of one object. Use Tabs.
The links jump within one long page. Use Toc.
The items are categories in a catalogue. Use ChipNav.

parts.name: children
parts.description: Slot: the component's content, given as the children of <cc-component>.

parts.name: subnav-item
parts.description: One page; a link or a button.

parts.name: subnav-meta
parts.description: A small count or badge at the end of the row.

components.name: Textarea
components.purpose: The input's skin on a native textarea. rows sets the starting height; data-fd-autogrow makes it grow with the text up to eight lines (data-max-rows changes that), then scroll. A counter in the field footer shows the limit when maxlength is set.
components.usage: Write an answer that runs over several lines. Also called: multiline input, text area, comment box, message box.
do: The answer is a sentence or more: a description, a prompt, a note.
The text length varies a lot and the field should grow with it (data-fd-autogrow).
dont: The value is one line. Use Input.
The text is code or JSON that needs checking. Use Codefield.
The value is a list with one item per line that should show as items. Use TagInput.
The value is names with values, one pair per line. Use Pairs.

props.name: size
props.description: Sets data-size. A compact note field in a dense panel.

props.name: autogrow
props.description: Sets data-fd-autogrow. Grows with its text, so people see all they wrote.

props.name: mono
props.description: Sets data-mono.

props.name: resize
props.description: Sets data-resize. The layout cannot take a drag handle.

components.name: Tooltip
components.purpose: One tooltip element serves the whole page. It waits 350ms the first time, then follows the pointer from one control to the next with no delay, and disappears on leave, press or scroll. Keyboard focus shows it at once. It never takes the pointer. Icon-only triggers without a name get the text as their aria-label.
components.usage: Name an icon-only control or reveal its shortcut on hover or focus. Also called: hint, title, hover text, tip, screen tip, label on hover, balloon.
do: An icon-only button needs a name.
A control has a keyboard shortcut to show (data-shortcut).
dont: The content has links or actions. Use Popover.
A preview of the thing a link points to. Use Hovercard.
The text is needed by everyone, such as a field label. Use Field.
A helper line under a form control. Use Field.

props.name: staticDemo
props.description: Sets data-static-demo.

parts.name: children
parts.description: Slot: the component's content, given as the children of <cc-component>.

parts.name: tooltip-keys
parts.description: The shortcut keys at the end.

components.name: Command
components.purpose: A modal search palette on Cmd+K or Ctrl+K. A search field over grouped, fuzzy-matched items with the matched letters lit. Items come from markup or from command.register(). Focus stays in the field; the active row is announced through aria-activedescendant.
components.usage: Jump to a page or run an action by typing, from anywhere. Also called: command palette, command bar, spotlight, quick open, omnibar, cmd-k, quick actions, go to anything.
do: An app has many pages and actions and power users want the keyboard.
People should reach a recent run, a doc or a setting without navigating.
Actions need shortcuts and hints shown beside them.
dont: Searching one list on one page. Use Search.
Choosing a value in a form. Use Combobox.
A short list of actions on one trigger. Use Menu.
Site-wide navigation that must always be visible. Use Sidebar.

props.name: staticDemo
props.description: Sets data-static-demo.

parts.name: children
parts.description: Slot: the component's content, given as the children of <cc-component>.

parts.name: command-item-hint
parts.description: A muted hint or shortcut at the end.

components.name: Icon
components.purpose: A 16px line icon from Fire's sprite, written as <i data-icon="name"> and drawn once at start (or as the fd-icon element with icon="name"). Sizes are 12, 14, 16, 20, 24 or 32 (plus sm and lg); tone sets its colour. It is decorative: name the control that holds it with a label. Change it with setIcon(el, name).
components.usage: Draw a small symbol beside a label or on a button. Also called: glyph, symbol, pictogram, svg icon, lucide.
do: A button, menu item or status needs a symbol to scan faster.
An empty state or a tile needs one glyph.
dont: The symbol is the only content and no label exists. Add an aria-label or data-fd-tooltip to the control that holds it.
A person's image is needed. Use Avatar.
A brand mark is needed. Use Brand.
A tile with a coloured background holds the glyph. Use Tile.

props.name: size
props.description: Sets data-size. Inside a dense chip or a badge.

props.name: tone
props.description: Sets data-tone. The icon marks the brand colour.

props.name: icon
props.description: Sets data-icon.

props.name: iconFill
props.description: Sets data-icon-fill.

props.name: nudge
props.description: Sets data-nudge. An arrow that moves a little on hover, for an external link.

components.name: Legend
components.purpose: A row of small swatches and muted labels. In a chart with data-legend it is a set of toggles: click a series to hide it and the scale adjusts; the last visible series cannot be turned off. To place one elsewhere, point a .fd-legend[data-for="#chart-id"] at the chart. Toggling fires fd:change.
components.usage: Say which colour means which series. Also called: key, chart key, series toggle, swatches, color key, chart legend.
do: A chart has two or more series and readers need to know which is which.
A custom layout needs the legend away from the chart.
Series must be switchable on and off.
dont: A donut: its legend is part of it. Use Donut.
A single series. Name the series in the card title instead.
A heat grid levels key. Use Heatgrid.

props.name: tone
props.description: Sets data-tone. A series that means failure.

parts.name: children
parts.description: Slot: the component's content, given as the children of <cc-component>.

parts.name: legend-item
parts.description: One series; a button when it toggles.

components.name: Matrix
components.purpose: A category by channel grid: a mono header row, one row per category and a fixed-width column per channel (data-cols 1 to 6). Each cell holds a switch or checkbox with an aria-label that names both the row and the column.
components.usage: Set one switch for each category and channel in a grid. Also called: notification table, permission grid, preference matrix, switch table.
do: Notification settings: events down the side, email, browser and phone across the top.
Permissions by role or by resource where every cell is on or off.
dont: There is one column of independent settings. Use Setting.
The grid shows data, not controls. Use Table.
Only one switch matters. Use Switch.

props.name: cols
props.description: Sets data-cols. One channel column.

parts.name: children
parts.description: Slot: the component's content, given as the children of <cc-component>.

parts.name: matrix-head
parts.description: The header row with channel names.

parts.name: matrix-text
parts.description: Holds the row label and description.

components.name: Pipeline
components.purpose: Staged work read left to right: stages in order, jobs in a stage run in parallel, and every job shows a status icon and a word for screen readers. It turns vertical in narrow containers. A job can be a button that selects, a link or plain text. A stage with data-when runs on a condition and joins by a dashed link. It is not a node editor.
components.usage: See what ran, what runs in parallel and what comes after, for one run. Also called: workflow, build pipeline, job graph, stages, DAG, CI pipeline, flow.
do: A crawl, deploy, data job or agent plan has stages and parallel jobs.
A run page lets people pick a failed job and read it beside the graph.
dont: Steps that run one after another. Use RunSteps.
The history of one thing. Use Timeline.
A free-form graph with arbitrary edges and dragging. Use a purpose-built graph library.
Progress with a total. Use Progress.

props.name: size
props.description: Sets data-size. Icon and name only, for cards and expanded rows.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Sets data-orientation. Force stacking at any width.

props.name: pipeline
props.description: Sets data-fd-pipeline.

parts.name: children
parts.description: Slot: the component's content, given as the children of <cc-component>.

parts.name: pipeline
parts.description: The block and its own container.

parts.name: pipeline-stage-label
parts.description: An optional label above a stage.

parts.name: pipeline-jobs
parts.description: The parallel jobs of a stage.

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.purpose: A list of links ending in the current page. Use it when a screen is several levels deep, such as a run inside a monitor. The last item is a span with aria-current="page". Wrap it in nav with aria-label="Breadcrumb".
components.usage: Show where this screen sits and jump to a parent. Also called: path, trail, hierarchy nav, location.
do: A screen is three or more levels deep and people need to go up to any parent.
The hierarchy is fixed: workspace, project, item.
dont: There is one obvious place to return to. Use Back.
The path is a flow in a set order. Use Steps.
Content is paged. Use Pagination.

parts.name: children
parts.description: Slot: the component's content, given as the children of <cc-component>.

parts.name: breadcrumb
parts.description: The nav; holds an ol of li items.

components.name: Combobox
components.purpose: A text field with a listbox that uses the Popover API, so it layers above everything and closes on outside clicks. Type to filter, arrow keys to move, Enter to choose. Options are role="option" rows with an optional icon, description and mono meta. The multiple variant keeps choices as removable tokens. Fires fd:open, fd:close, fd:select and fd:change.
components.usage: Pick from a long list by typing to filter it. Also called: autocomplete, typeahead, combo box, searchable select, multiselect, dropdown search.
do: The list is long enough that people need to type to find an item.
Each option needs an icon, a description or a meta label (a model, a team member).
Several items may be chosen and shown as tokens (data-multiple).
dont: The list is short and plain. Use Select.
People may enter values that are not on a list. Use TagInput.
The choice runs a command or jumps to a page. Use Command.
The options are two to four visible labels. Use Segmented.

parts.name: children
parts.description: Slot: the component's content, given as the children of <cc-component>.

parts.name: combobox
parts.description: The wrapper; carries data-fd-combobox and data-name.

components.name: Donut
components.purpose: A thin ring for two to five segments with the total in the centre and a legend beside it. Hover a segment or a legend row to read it in the centre. In data-type="progress" it is a progress ring: one value against a known end, such as an import. A quota or limit is a meter, not a ring.
components.usage: Show parts of a whole, or one value against a known end. Also called: pie chart, doughnut, ring chart, radial chart, share chart, circular progress, proportion.
do: A share of a whole has two to five parts: requests by endpoint, credits by team.
A single progress value needs a larger ring with a label in the middle.
dont: Use against a quota or a limit. Use Meter.
More than five parts, or parts that must be compared closely. Use Bars.
A value over time. Use Chart.
A small inline ring beside text. Use Progress.

props.name: tone

components.name: Fab
components.purpose: A 48px round accent button with a soft shadow that floats at a screen corner: a support chat, scroll to bottom. It grows slightly on hover and shrinks on press. Position it with your own layout; it has no label, so give it aria-label.
components.usage: Keep one primary action in reach while the page scrolls. Also called: floating action button, FAB, floating button, speed dial, support bubble.
do: One action is useful on every part of a long screen, such as opening support.
A phone screen has one main create action that must stay visible.
dont: The action belongs in a toolbar or a footer. Use Button.
The launcher opens a chat window. Use ChatLauncher.
There are several actions. Use Menu.
An action is part of a form. Use Button.

components.name: Hovercard
components.purpose: A card that opens after half a second of hovering a link, stays open while the pointer travels into it, and closes a quarter second after leaving. It holds a title, meta, a line of text and a few stats. It is not for actions or forms.
components.usage: Preview a link's target, such as a person or a provider, without leaving the page. Also called: preview card, peek, profile card, link preview, user card, hover preview.
do: A name in a table or sentence links to a person, provider or run and a quick look saves a click.
Preview facts are read-only: a role, counts, a date.
dont: The content has actions, inputs or links people must click. Use Popover.
Naming an icon button or a shortcut. Use Tooltip.
The preview is needed on touch devices. Use Sheet.
A short list of choices. Use Menu.

components.name: Notification
components.purpose: A row in the notifications popover: a title, a line of text and a time, with an accent dot when unread. The popover has Mark all read, an All / Unread switch, a category select and an empty state. The count on the bell follows the unread rows through data-fd-unread-count.
components.usage: Read the list of things that happened, with the unread ones marked. Also called: inbox, alerts, bell, activity feed, notification centre, updates, unread list.
do: A bell opens a list of finished jobs, monitor changes and billing alerts.
Items must be marked read one by one or all at once.
dont: A short confirmation that vanishes. Use Toast.
A message about the account on every page. Use Banner.
A history of one object. Use Timeline.
A table of records. Use List.

components.name: Pagination
components.purpose: A count on the left and joined previous and next buttons on the right: "Page 1 of 12" or "Showing 51-100 of 2,481". The numbered variant adds page numbers and gaps for people who jump to a page they remember.
components.usage: Move through a list that is split into pages. Also called: pager, paging, page navigation, prev next.
do: A log, table or result list is split into pages of fixed size.
People move forward and back far more often than they jump.
dont: Content loads as people scroll. Load more as the list ends; no component is needed.
The items are steps in a flow. Use Steps.
The views are different objects. Use Tabs.

props.name: variant
props.description: Sets data-variant. People jump to a page they remember.

components.name: Radio
components.purpose: A native radio with an accent ring and a dot that scales in with a slight spring. Group the options in role="radiogroup" with a label. The label is part of the control. It is for one choice from two to four plain options saved with the form.
components.usage: Choose exactly one option from a few. Also called: radio button, option button, single choice.
do: One of 2 to 4 options is saved with the form and each has a short label.
Options should all stay visible so people compare them.
dont: Two options behave like on and off. Use Switch.
Each option needs a title, a sentence or a price. Use Choice.
The options filter or switch what is shown right here. Use Segmented.
There are more than four or five options. Use Select.

parts.name: radio

components.name: Toc
components.purpose: An "On this page" list beside long reference content. With data-fd-scrollspy a marker follows the scroll and the current item gets aria-current="true". Items are anchors to section ids; data-level="2" indents sub-sections. fd:change fires when the current section changes.
components.usage: List the sections of a long page and follow the reader. Also called: table of contents, on this page, anchor links, scrollspy, page outline.
do: A long documentation or reference page has several sections.
People jump to a section and need to know where they are.
dont: The links go to other pages. Use Subnav.
The views replace each other. Use Tabs.
The page is short. Leave it out; headings are enough.

components.name: Texture
components.purpose: Fire's signature: letters and punctuation whose density follows a generated field, at very low contrast (under 1.6:1) and always decorative. A field fills its positioned parent behind the content. Fields are seeded by name so a page always looks the same, animate at 12 frames a second where they should, pause off-screen and stand still under reduced motion. Also holds dot grids, registration marks, grain and glyphs.
components.usage: Add a quiet generated field of characters, dots or marks behind a hero, banner or empty state. Also called: ascii art, background pattern, noise, grain, dot grid, hero background, generative art, backdrop.
do: A page hero, a launch banner or an empty state needs depth without adding anything to read.
A single object needs the page frame's registration marks.
An empty state needs a small accent glyph above its title.
dont: The decoration would sit behind paragraphs, tables, forms or code. Leave the surface plain.
A status that shows live work. Use Loader.
The surface needs to say something, such as an announcement. Use Announce.
A chart or a data picture. Use Chart.

components.name: App
components.purpose: The app shell: a sidebar on the left, a main column with the top bar and the page, and a mobile nav. The sidebar is expanded or a 64px icon rail; the choice is remembered. The shell is a size container, so under 900px of its own width the sidebar gives way to the top bar and a menu button. It also holds the floating support button.
components.usage: Frame every signed-in screen with a sidebar, a top bar and a page. Also called: app shell, layout, dashboard layout, admin layout, scaffold, chrome, main layout.
do: The product has several screens that share navigation, an account and a top bar.
A screen is a working page inside the product, not a single task on its own page.
dont: A single task on a page of its own: sign in, consent, a result. Use Screen.
A docs site with its own two-row top bar and contents column. Use Doc.
A marketing page with no signed-in navigation. Use Page.

components.name: Page
components.purpose: The page holds a centred column with 1px rails; each fd-band is a horizontal strip, separated by hairlines that run edge to edge, with a crosshair where a line meets a rail. Bands set padding, surface and whether they grow. On phones the rails and marks drop away and only the hairlines remain.
components.usage: Lay a page out as a drafted column cut into bands by hairlines. Also called: page layout, section, band, container, content area, main.
do: Any screen in the app: one band for the title, one for the toolbar, one for the content.
A band needs a white or sunken surface, a different padding, or to stick under the top bar.
dont: Cards or groups inside one band. Use Card.
Two columns of content inside a band. Use Split.
A grid of equal tiles. Use Grid.

components.name: Tile
components.purpose: A square holder, 36px by default, that steps through 20, 28, 40, 44 and 56 with a growing radius. It holds an image, an icon or letters. Tone tints it; data-shape gives a circle or a wide stat tile. Use letter tiles or glyphs for providers, not brand colours.
components.usage: Hold a logo, a glyph or one or two letters in a square. Also called: icon tile, logo holder, app icon, glyph, letter tile, icon box, logo mark.
do: A row or card needs a mark for what it is: a provider, an integration, a key type.
A feature list or empty state needs a leading icon holder.
dont: The mark is a person. Use Avatar.
A label next to a word. Use Badge.
A figure with a label. Use Stats.
A bare icon beside text. Use Icon.

components.name: Card
components.purpose: A white surface with a 1px faint edge and no shadow at rest. Head, body and foot are optional parts; the foot sticks to the bottom when cards share a row. data-interactive makes the whole card a link or button. Cards never nest.
components.usage: Group the parts of one object on a quiet surface. Also called: tile, panel, box, surface, content card, provider card, link card.
do: One object (a key, a team, a plan, a provider) has a title, some facts and an action.
A catalogue shows many similar things in a grid: use fd-card-grid.
The whole card opens a page: add data-interactive and fd-card-arrow.
dont: A figure with a disclosure of detail, such as credits remaining. Use DataCard.
A set of headline numbers in a row. Use Stats.
A single pricing option with a price and features. Use Plan.
Rows that are mostly text and one action. Use List.
A section inside a card needs structure. Use a hairline, never a card inside a card.

components.name: Callout
components.purpose: A tinted message with an icon, a title, a short body and usually one action. It belongs to the content around it. Tone sets the meaning: neutral, accent, success, warning, danger, info, violet. It can be dismissed, and a dismissal can be remembered.
components.usage: Tell the reader what happened and what to do, next to the content it is about. Also called: alert, notice, admonition, inline message, info box, hint box, message bar.
do: A form or section needs a warning, a tip or a result right beside it.
An error has a cause and a next step the reader can take.
A limit is close: credits at 90%, crawl depth capped on the plan.
dont: The message affects the whole account and fits in one line. Use Banner.
The message confirms something that just happened and should fade away. Use Toast.
A field has an invalid value. Use Field.
A list or table has nothing to show. Use Empty.

props.name: size
props.description: Sets data-size. A single-line callout: title and text run together.

props.name: tone
props.description: Sets data-tone. Callout: neutral news or guidance.

components.name: Codeblock
components.purpose: A framed block on a sunken well with a header and a pre. Fire tokenises JSON, shell and cURL, JavaScript and TypeScript, and Python; unknown text stays plain. The header holds a filename or language tabs, never both. Options: line numbers, a highlighted range, a folded height, soft wrap. Copy takes the raw text.
components.usage: Show code a developer will read or paste, with copy, line numbers and language tabs. Also called: code snippet, syntax highlighting, code sample, pre, source view, code fence, code panel.
do: A request, a config or a response is shown in docs or a detail panel.
The same request is offered in several languages: use tabs; the choice syncs across the page.
A long response should start folded with a "Show all" button.
dont: One command or one value to copy. Use Snippet.
A response people explore and fold. Use Json.
A change between two versions. Use Diff.
Streaming lines with levels and search. Use Log.
Code inside a sentence. Use InlineCode.

components.name: PageHero
components.purpose: A tall title band for the screens people reach from the sidebar: an eyebrow, the screen name, one line of what it is for, and an art slot that fades toward the text and holds an ASCII texture. Page-wide actions go in fd-page-hero-actions at the end of the title row (at most one primary) and drop under the line when there is no room.
components.usage: Open a top-level screen with a tall title band and one line about it. Also called: hero, banner, page banner, title band, masthead, section header, jumbotron.
do: A top-level screen, such as Monitoring or Settings, opens a section of the product.
The page has an action for the whole page: connect, get the code, export everything.
dont: A working page under a section, where space matters. Use PageHead.
A create button that belongs to one list. Use Toolbar.
A single task outside the shell. Use Screen.

components.name: Status
components.purpose: A dot and a word. Only a running item pulses, and only while it is running (data-live). The icon variant swaps the dot for a status icon that spins while live; the pill variant puts the state in a tinted pill.
components.usage: Show the state of a run, a monitor or a key with a dot and a word. Also called: state, indicator, health, status dot, status pill, run state.
do: A row needs the state of a thing: Running, Passed, Failed, Paused.
A header shows the state of the page object as a tinted pill.
dont: A label that is not a state: a plan, a role, a count. Use Badge.
Several jobs with durations in a graph. Use Pipeline.
Progress of work with a known total. Use Progress.
A dot on a person. Use Avatar.

components.name: Skeleton
components.purpose: Grey blocks that have the exact geometry of what they stand in for, so the real content swaps in without a line moving. Parts: text lines, titles by type role, avatar, button and tile. Presets for cards, grids, tables, stats, charts, lists, threads, forms, a hero and a whole page fill themselves from an empty element. Skeletons are aria-hidden; set aria-busy on the container.
components.usage: Hold a place for content that is loading, with the same shape as the real thing. Also called: loading placeholder, shimmer, ghost loader, content loader, loading state, placeholder blocks.
do: A region has a known layout and its data is on the way.
A route paints for the first time and the page needs rail, top bar and table in place.
Content swaps in place: wrap skeleton and content in data-fd-loading and call setLoading(el, false).
dont: A small control or one line of text. Use Loader.
Navigation between pages. Use Pagebar.
The request failed; say what failed. Use Empty.
The page is empty on purpose. Use Empty.

parts.description: Text lines of varied widths that end at 60%; data-lines sets how many.

parts.name: skeleton-card

parts.name: skeleton-list

components.name: Snippet
components.purpose: A one-line well with a mono value and a copy button: an install line, a skill URL, a key. The $ prompt is decoration and is never copied. fd-snippet-em marks the one segment that matters; fd-snippet-dim quiets the rest. Numbered steps put a title, a hint and a snippet under each number; a done step shows a check.
components.usage: Copy one command or one value, or follow a short list of numbered commands. Also called: command, install command, copy command, one-liner, shell command, terminal command, copy box, setup steps.
do: A reader leaves with one command: install, login, run.
Setup takes several commands that should be numbered.
A key or skill URL shows in an accent well.
dont: Several lines of code or a file. Use Codeblock.
A secret that stays hidden until revealed. Use Secret.
A form field the reader can edit. Use CopyField.
Code inside a sentence. Use InlineCode.

A toolbar adds a label, size, Expand all, Collapse all and Copy.
components.usage: Explore a JSON response by folding it, not by reading it whole. Also called: JSON viewer, tree view, object inspector, JSON explorer, collapsible JSON, response viewer.
do: A response is explored rather than copied whole.
People need the path to a nested value.
A result offers a Table | JSON switch of the same data.
dont: A short request or a config to copy. Use Codeblock.
Records with the same fields. Use Table.
Parameter docs. Use Schema.
A diff between two JSON documents. Use Diff.

components.name: Badge

A value is a state in a table cell: Success, Failed, Queued.
A small count sits next to a tab, a menu item or a bell.

The state is the point of the row and a dot and word read better. Use Status.
The message is a full sentence. Use Callout.
The mark means an account or a link is verified. Use Verified.

components.name: Empty

A search or filter matches nothing; say what to change.
A request failed and the reader can retry.
A feature is not on the plan; say which plan has it.
dont: The message is a warning above content that exists. Use Callout.
Data is on its way. Use Skeleton.
A chart has no data in the range. Use Chart.
A table needs the same states inside its frame. Use Table.

components.name: Panel

do: Details sit beside the thing they describe and need a head.
A screen is built around a list of sessions or items in its own column.
dont: The content is an object in a grid or list. Use Card.
A temporary surface that opens over the page. Use Sheet.
Settings for one group inside a form. Use FormSection.

props.description: Sets data-variant. A fixed 320px column next to the rail that holds a list, such as sessions.

parts.name: children

components.name: Split

components.usage: Put details beside the thing they describe, in two columns. Also called: two-column layout, master-detail, sidebar layout, aside layout, detail pane, inspector layout.
do: A list or run needs a details panel beside it.
Settings pages have a section nav at the start and a form beside it.

components.name: ChatMessage
components.purpose: One message in a chat. The person speaks from a grey bubble on the right, the AI in prose beside a spark, a person from support in a white bubble beside their face, and the system in small muted lines. Messages from one author within two minutes join into a run. The body is a stack of blocks, each built from another Fire component. Only the latest message of the person shows its delivery state.
components.usage: Show who said what in a chat, and carry blocks such as forms, cards and approvals. Also called: chat bubble, chat turn, support message, rich message, message block, quick replies, chat card.
do: A support or help chat shows turns from the person, the AI, an agent and the system.
An answer should hold a form, a card, a list of choices or an approval, not only text.
dont: A turn in an agent thread. Use Message.
A notification outside a conversation. Use Notification.
A single tool step. Use Toolcall.

voice.tone: Plain, specific, direct, calm and honest. The screen is the explanation and words fill only the gaps. Second person, active voice, present tense. Developers think in endpoints, keys, credits and requests: use those words, with identifiers in mono. No exclamation marks, no "Oops", no padding "please" or "sorry".
do: Name tasks by what the person does and places by what they are: "Scrape a page", "API keys".
Give every button a verb or a verb and its object ("Create key", "Export CSV"); the primary button in a dialog repeats the dialog title's verb.
Replace adjectives with facts: numbers, names, dates ("about 2 seconds", "Nov 23", "1,520 credits").
Say each thing once: if the title says "API keys", the description does not begin "API keys are".
Write errors as what happened, then what to do: "Couldn't reach docs.example.com. Check the URL, or try again in a minute."
Write empty states as a short title, one sentence saying what will appear, and one action.
Use sentence case; titles, labels and buttons have no full stop, descriptions and errors do.
Set identifiers (keys, IDs, paths, endpoints, file names) in mono and never reword them.
Confirm only what cannot be undone or costs money; otherwise act and offer Undo.
Name one thing one way across the interface, the docs and the API (Create, Add, Remove, Delete, Revoke).
dont: Do not write "OK", "Submit", "Yes", "Click here" or a bare "Continue" on a button.
Do not use simply, just, easily, quickly, successfully, basically, actually or very.
Do not restate the title, the label or the value in a description or hint.
Do not blame the person ("You entered an invalid URL") or show a raw status code as the whole error.
Do not put anything a person must read to finish the task in a tooltip.
Do not list the allowed answers in a hint under a text box: the control is wrong, use a select, segmented control or switch.
Do not describe emptiness ("There is nothing here") or apologise in an empty state.
Do not stack callouts: one that interrupts is useful, three mean none matter.
Do not invent product names for ordinary things.
